minimal_install_proposal:
Today's mechanics are already close to minimal and don't need a new command surface — they need the missing back half wired up. Proposed steady state, verified against what I actually ran:

macOS/Linux, pi/Claude Code/Codex users:
  pip install vacant-network
  vacant install
  <open your usual agent, work as normal>

Windows / anyone who wants OpenCode's non-TUI path covered too: same two lines; OpenCode's
`opencode run` still needs the wrapper-redo fallback (`vacant do opencode`) since it has no
Stop hook to push back through — that's a real per-agent ceiling, not a missing install step,
and should be documented as such rather than hidden.

Two commands, zero flags, zero prompts, zero contract file, zero keys typed — that's what I
measured: `pip install` (32s here, 36 packages, matches README's own "30 wheels/60MB" note)
then `vacant install` (sub-second, prints one line per agent, exit 0 whether or not any agent
binary exists). No third step is needed once VACANT_MODE defaults to "evidence" with no
contract present (see zero_config_blockers) — `vacant install` already detects agents via
`shutil.which` and writes only the two per-agent files (extension/hook + skill) with no
interaction, so the "install" side of "minimal install" is essentially done; what's missing is
that step 2 currently installs hooks that, when they fire, do nothing (Stop returns bare allow)
because nothing in the code reads a non-existent contract as "run the zero-config evidence
pass instead." Making that default is the single change that turns "vacant install" from a
no-op-until-you-write-a-contract into the "install once, keep using your agent, get checked
results" product described in CLAUDE.md's 產品原則.

Concretely, minimal code changes to reach that minimal install:
1. `VACANT_MODE` (off/observe/persona/evidence) read from env, default written into
   `install.json` at `vacant install` time as `evidence` — new, ~80 lines (per arch.md
   new_pieces #1).
2. `trace/capture.py::workspace_for`: trace the project (git toplevel or cwd) whenever mode !=
   off, not only when a contract exists or VACANT_TRACE=1 — small change to an existing
   condition, verified today's condition by direct read (`workspace_for`) and by observing that
   `VACANT_TRACE=1` alone already produces a real signed chain, so the plumbing this depends on
   already works; it's just gated wrong.
3. `adapters/hook.py::handle`: when `ev.kind == "stop"` and `contract is None` but mode !=
   off, call a new `decide_stop_zero` (evidence-based) instead of returning allow —
   confirmed today's exact gate by reading and by running a live stop hook call, which returned
   `{"action":"allow","reason":""}` with a full trace chain present.
4. The rest of arch.md's `new_pieces` (evidence.py, derive.py, evidence_rules.json,
   projectchecks.py, review.py, delivery.py, final-assistant-text forwarding, feedback-header
   recognition) is what makes the redo useful rather than a no-op stop-through — the CLAUDE.md
   size estimate (~2,700 lines + ~200 tests) stands; I did not find anything in the shipped
   code that shortcuts it.
5. Two small, install-mechanics-only fixes I found by actually running the flow, not in
   study_result.json's new_pieces: register the adapter/intake/trace subcommands as real
   argparse subparsers (or add a "see also" line) so `vacant --help` actually lists `install`
   (today it silently doesn't, confirmed); and have `vacant install`'s own output, or the
   README, mention `~/.local/bin` PATH the way pip's own warning already does, since a
   zero-config user hits that PATH gap before they ever reach a Vacant prompt.

Nothing about the *install mechanics* needs to shrink further — one pip line, one vacant line,
no interactive prompts, additive+reversible file writes, clean uninstall. The "minimal install"
the human is asking for is already built; what's missing is making that minimal install do
something by default.
what_install_writes:
Verified hands-on in a clean container (python:3.11-slim, non-root `tester` user, pi 0.87.1
installed via npm, wheel built from repo HEAD b8b78304):

`pip install --user vacant-network` (or the wheel): 36 packages into
`~/.local/lib/python3.11/site-packages` (48MB), console scripts `vacant` and `vacant-network`
into `~/.local/bin` (not on PATH by default — pip prints its own warning about this; the
README's quickstart block doesn't). No files outside site-packages/bin; no prompts; no network
calls beyond the package download itself; no keys.

`vacant install` (no agent binaries on PATH): prints
`<agent>: not installed on this machine — skipped` for each of pi/Claude Code/OpenCode/Codex,
writes exactly one file: `~/.vacant/adapters/install.json` = `{"agents": {}}`. No prompt, exit
0.

`vacant install` (pi present, the only agent I could get running in this container — node
version blocked Claude/Codex/OpenCode's own CLIs from being fully exercised, not a Vacant
issue): writes exactly two files —
`~/.pi/agent/extensions/vacant.ts` (159 lines; a thin bridge that spawns
`<same python interpreter used to install vacant_network> -m vacant_network hook pi <event>`
per pi lifecycle event, with per-event timeouts and "any failure = allow" fail-open behavior so
a broken hook can't hang or block pi) and `~/.pi/agent/skills/vacant/SKILL.md`. Both are
recorded, with sha256 and a "was this file pre-existing" flag, in
`~/.vacant/adapters/install.json` for exact, reversible undo. No prompt, no network call, exit
0.

First hook invocation that reaches the intake layer (even a bare `stop` event) silently
generates four long-term Ed25519 keypairs — owner/approver/reviewer/verifier — under
`~/.vacant/intake/keys/*/identity.{key,pub}` with correct restrictive permissions (0700 dirs,
0600 private keys), plus `~/.vacant/intake/trust.json` recording their fingerprints and
`~/.vacant/intake/keys.lock`. No prompt, nothing printed to the user announcing this happened;
verified by direct filesystem diff before/after a single hook call.

With no `vacant.toml` contract and `VACANT_TRACE` unset (the actual zero-config default today),
a `stop` hook event writes exactly one JSON line to `~/.vacant/intake/hooks/events.jsonl` and
returns `{"action":"allow","reason":""}` — confirmed by running it directly with a
`last_assistant_message` claiming "tests pass" against a workspace that had never run tests;
nothing caught it, nothing recorded beyond that one log line. Setting `VACANT_TRACE=1`
(undocumented in the quickstart) turns on real per-step chain recording under
`~/.vacant/trace/projects/<key>/{chain.ndjson,head.json,state.json,perf.jsonl}` plus
content-addressed blobs under `~/.vacant/trace/objects/` — but even with that full chain
present, the Stop check itself still returned bare "allow", confirming the gate is on contract
presence, not trace presence.

No API keys, model credentials or network endpoints are ever requested or written by any of
the above; nothing in this whole flow makes an outbound network call except the initial `pip
install` package download and (later) the `npm install -g` I ran to get a real pi binary for
testing agent detection.
zero_config_blockers: VACANT_MODE (off/observe/persona/evidence) does not exist anywhere in the codebase — `grep -rn VACANT_MODE vacant_network/` returns zero hits. There is no install-time or env-level switch that turns on zero-config behavior at all; it's a design proposal in study_result.json's arch object, not shipped code.

adapters/hook.py::handle's Stop branch is gated on `contract is not None`; verified live by piping a stop event with no vacant.toml into `python3 -m vacant_network hook pi stop` — it returns bare {"action":"allow","reason":""} regardless of what the agent's final message claims, even when a full signed trace chain exists for that session (VACANT_TRACE=1 case). No contract => nothing is ever checked, by design of the current code, not by bug.

trace/capture.py::workspace_for only traces a project when a contract exists OR VACANT_TRACE=1 is explicitly set — and VACANT_TRACE is not set by `vacant install`, not documented in the README quickstart, and not read from any per-install config. Zero-config installs today record essentially nothing (one JSONL line per hook event) unless a user independently discovers and sets an undocumented env var.

adapters/run.py (the `vacant do` no-hooks alternative the README also advertises as a zero-hooks path) is typed around Contract throughout (`task.contract`, `task.contract.max_attempts`, contract-relative workspace prep) — it is not a contract-free path either, contrary to how the README's 'also can run without any hooks' phrasing reads to a new user.

The evidence pass itself (unread_material / unsourced_value / write_before_read / unbacked_test_claim / failed_step_ignored / project_check checks, ~650 lines per arch.md's own estimate) does not exist; trace/evidence.py is not present in the repo. Without it there is nothing for a zero-config Stop hook to check even if the contract gate above were removed.

hookpolicy.decide_stop (the round-cap / push-back state machine) only has a contract-keyed variant; the design's decide_stop_zero (keyed on session+workspace instead of session+contract-path) does not exist, so there is no round-cap or new_request-reset logic for a contract-less project.

There is no delivery-note mechanism (trace/delivery.py per the design) — nothing produces the Checked/Fixed/Unverified note CLAUDE.md's 產品原則 and the human's own words in LOOP.md §一之二 require at the end of a zero-config run; today's `systemMessage`/report paths are contract-report outputs only.

Final-assistant-text is not forwarded from pi (event.context.llmMessages) or OpenCode (SDK session messages) into Vacant's capture layer — confirmed by reading adapters/agents.py, which today only handles the Stop-continuation push-back path, not text capture for the unbacked_test_claim check the design needs.

OpenCode's `opencode run` (non-interactive/non-TUI use) has no Stop hook at all — confirmed in this session's own evidence dir (e2e_trace: 'feedback reached model = False' in all rows) and unchanged as of this read. Zero-config for OpenCode's headless mode structurally requires the wrapper-redo fallback (`vacant do`/Harbor wrapper), not the hook path, and any zero-config design that assumes uniform hook coverage across all four agents is wrong for this one case.

`vacant --help` does not list `install`/`uninstall`/`contract`/`do`/`hook`/`trace`/`flag` at all (verified live) — they're dispatched by checking argv[0] against hardcoded tuples before argparse's own parser (which drives --help) ever sees them. A brand-new zero-config user's first command, `vacant --help`, does not lead them to the commands the README's quickstart tells them to run next.

uninstall:
Two independent 'uninstall' verbs today, both verified live, neither one complete on its own:

1. `vacant uninstall` reverses only what `vacant install` wrote to agent config: it walked the
   two ops I had it record for pi (the `vacant.ts` extension file and the `SKILL.md` skill
   file), removed both, and reset `~/.vacant/adapters/install.json` back to `{"agents": {}}`.
   Nothing else under `~/.pi` (or the other three agents' config dirs) was touched. Exit 0, no
   prompt. This matches the "key-level, reversible, only-what-we-wrote" design described in
   adapters/install.py's own module docstring — I confirmed it in practice, not just by
   reading the comment: it correctly distinguishes "we created this file" (delete outright)
   from "we appended to an existing file the user already had" (restore the pre-install bytes
   from backup, verified against the recorded sha256 so a since-edited file is never silently
   clobbered).

2. `pip uninstall -y vacant-network` removes the Python package (site-packages, console
   scripts) cleanly — verified: `vacant` disappears from PATH immediately after. This is
   ordinary pip behavior, not a Vacant-specific mechanism, and it does **not** know about or
   touch `$VACANT_HOME`.

Neither command removes `~/.vacant` (`$VACANT_HOME`): after both of the above, 176KB remained
on disk — the four long-term signing keypairs, the trace chain objects and state from the one
test project, install.json, intake trust/lock state. A user who wants to fully remove all
trace of having tried Vacant has to know to `rm -rf ~/.vacant` (or `$VACANT_HOME` if they set
it) themselves; nothing in the CLI says so. This is a small, cheap fix (a `--purge` flag on
`vacant uninstall`, or a printed hint after it runs) but it is a real gap in "uninstall" as
experienced by a real user, found only by actually running both uninstall paths and diffing
the filesystem before/after — recommend adding it alongside the other install-mechanics fixes
above (--help discoverability, PATH hint) since all three are copy the exact same shape of
gap: the mechanism is fine, the user just isn't told about the one manual step still needed.
